subject.title: [Feature]: Optimization for Dockerfile.sandbox-common # add retries and fix-missings for apt-get

question: Should sandbox Dockerfile resilience be implemented as retry-only APT behavior, or may install commands use `--fix-missing` with explicit package verification?
rationale: The central request is valid as a build-reliability improvement, but `--fix-missing` changes package-install failure semantics and needs owner intent before a fix can be considered best.

options.title: Use retry-only APT behavior
options.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries` for transient network failures while preserving fail-closed package installation; this is the narrowest safer path.

options.title: Accept `--fix-missing` with verification
options.body: Allow partial retrieval semantics only if the Dockerfiles verify required packages or commands after install and maintainers intentionally own that contract.

options.title: Decline Dockerfile resilience change
options.body: Leave the current fail-fast Dockerfiles unchanged if maintainers decide the extra build-time behavior is not worth carrying.

recommendation.title: Use retry-only APT behavior
recommendation.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries` for transient network failures while preserving fail-closed package installation; this is the narrowest safer path.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has recent Docker build-cache history and handled the earlier same-request PR closure, making him a practical routing owner for the product/validation decision.
